shared_mechanism.summary: The census rows about the notice board and its caption are one design, and the future-work record already says why: 'No seat search can fix that, because the board is in the wrong PLACE to be captioned, and nine attempts inside the search is what it cost to see that' (siting.py:436-443; future-work/farming-communities.md, 'ATTEMPTS 8-13'). The one placer never refuses. It takes the least-cost seat (placer.py:283-289) or the first seat off the frame (placer.py:285-287), because the GM rules labels mandatory ('we'll treat labels as mandatory'). So a caption rule cannot be guaranteed inside place() by dropping the caption. It is guaranteed by the placer that decides the SUBJECT: the board siter accepts only a board seat whose caption the one placer can seat clean.
pieces: labels/placer.py: add `place(..., strict=True)`, which returns None where the lax version would take the least-cost seat or the off-frame `first` seat. Lax stays the default for the standard's mandatory-label callers.

labels/obstacles.py: `ObstacleIndex.cost(..., own_gap=...)`. For a point subject, an obstacle at or nearer than the block's gap to its own subject counts (the association rule, standard.py 'ASSOCIATION'). Today only CLEAR_EM does, and a ring>0 seat lets a neighbor stand nearer.

settlement/structures/captions.py:label_obstacles adds (a) every drawn tree crown (`tree_crowns`, the canopy_index source) as an Obstacle with group 'grove', so a caption naming trees may lie on it and no other caption may, and (b) the record box of every still-QUEUED fixed-seat `text` caption, so a probe made at siting time sees every caption the label phase will have drawn before this one.

One predicate, `board_caption_seat(M-or-s, x, y, hw, hh, rot, label, index, frame) -> Placement | None`: `place(strict=True)` at the angle the board will be drawn at (nearest_way_bearing). It replaces board_caption_level's three levels and the older probes (label_seat_clear / `lab`, caption_lane_clearance) that disagree with the placer (FR-003).

The siter keeps only seats where board_caption_seat is not None. The Placement it proved rides in the queued `kosatsuba` payload, and _draw_board_caption draws that Placement. On a hamlet the board caption is the only caption and stage_labels follows stage_notice with nothing between them (row 8 notes; frame.py stage order). The drawn seat is therefore the probed one by construction, not a re-search against a different index (the 'later stage' named in rows 1, 2 and 4).
shared_mechanism.one_siter: hamletgen/frame.py:stage_notice's re-seat (frame.py:190-369) exists only because place_kosatsuba samples seats outside the view. place_kosatsuba already runs after stage_frame and already reads meta.view (siting.py:295-296). So the view, inset by the board's half-diagonal, becomes a CANDIDATE filter in place_kosatsuba, and the re-seat is deleted with its `loose` and pragma-no-cover branches (R2 rows 15 and 16). One siter applies every board rule once, instead of two siters restating them with drift (the re-seat's own comments record four such drifts: features 154, 227, 230, 261).

The predicates are the test's own: `RouteReach(departure_routes(M)).missed(x, y, band)` (the same body as routes_missed) and `kosatsuba_anchor`. They run BEFORE the knob is committed: the candidate set is computed per placement value, and `kosatsuba_affordances(M)` gains `entrance_sitable` (non-empty after these filters and the caption filter L4-L7). resolve_knob therefore never rolls `entrance` on a map that cannot site it.

rules.owner: l7r/diagram/labels/obstacles.py:ObstacleIndex.cost (new own_gap term), called by labels/placer.py:place for point subjects
rules.mechanism: place() computes `own_gap = poly_gap(block, subject.poly)` per point candidate and passes it to cost(). An obstacle counts when its gap to the block is <= max(clear, own_gap), not just < clear. At ring 0 this closes the tie the test's strict `>` forbids (both at CLEAR_EM). At ring > 0 it refuses a seat a neighbor stands nearer than the board. This is the placer's own rule for EVERY point caption (a stricter reading of the standard's association clause, no new form), so strict=True makes it a refusal. The test's comparison set becomes label_obstacles' built records (vw/vh as drawn, not w/h), the one predicate.
rules.unit_test: A board with a byre whose edge stands 5 ft from the board's upper-right ring-2 seat while ring 0/1 seats are blocked by a house. Assert the ring-2 seat is refused (cost > 0), and that a placement returned under strict has own_gap < every other obstacle's gap. Plus a tie case: an obstacle exactly CLEAR_EM from a ring-0 block is counted.
rules.risk_why: The own_gap term changes place() for every point caption (hand sheets, compounds, the board). Hand-sheet captions that took a ring>0 cost-0 seat beside a nearer neighbor will move (feature 286's measured sheets). Their re-render must be checked.

rules.mechanism: Every tree crown (tree_crowns, falling back to grove clumps, the same source as canopy_index) becomes an Obstacle(circle-as-poly, WEIGHT_OBSTACLE, group='grove'). place() then prefers a crown-clear seat among all ranked seats instead of accepting the first roof-clear one and asking about crowns afterwards. strict=True refuses a crown seat, and board_caption_seat's None refuses the board seat. The predicate is quad_on_canopy's circle test expressed as the index's poly_gap: one reading, and the test calls the index. meta.kosatsuba_caption_level is dropped. It recorded a level-1 compromise that can no longer be emitted.

rules.rule: A caption is never drawn without recording the box of the feature it names (element [6]; caption_stands_beside_its_referent).
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/finish.py:Settlement.label / _record_label (the census named captions.py:_draw_seated_caption, which holds it only for seated captions)
rules.mechanism: Seated captions always pass ref=subject_ref(...). On the `text` path, label() gets `ref` as a required keyword whose only non-box value is an explicit sentinel `NO_REFERENT`, allowed only for district/area-name captions. _record_label writes the box or, for the sentinel, the caption's own area box. No caller can emit a caption with ref=None, so the rule is a property of the call signature, not of which stages happen to call it. The live hamlet path is unchanged. The legacy town/city callers (funerary.py, ground.py, trades.py, castle_civic.py) pass the sentinel or their box: a signature edit that places nothing, within the spec's code-path line.
rules.fallback: None: a missing referent is a TypeError at the call site, a programming contract caught by the type checker and the unit test, not a map-time refusal.
rules.unit_test: label(x, y, 'the well') with no ref raises TypeError. With ref=(...) the queued payload and the drawn record carry it. The seated path records subject_ref for point, line and area subjects.
rules.risk_why: A signature change. No live map changes.

rules.rule: A caption never stands more than HUG_PX (120 px) box-to-box from the feature it names (label_hugs_its_referent).
rules.mechanism: Bounded by construction today but implicitly (REACH_EM*size + NUDGE_PX*sqrt2). HUG_PX moves into labels/standard.py beside REACH_EM, and rings(size) caps the last ring at `HUG_PX - NUDGE_PX*sqrt(2)`, so no point or line candidate, extended or nudged, can exceed it at any caption size. An area caption lies inside its subject (gap 0, or its inside test is a cost). The `first` off-frame fallback is ring 0. The one predicate is `hug_gap(block, ref_box)` (the test's _box_gap), which the placer's unit test and any caller read.
rules.fallback: None needed: no candidate lies beyond the cap.
rules.unit_test: For sizes 7, 8, 9, 15 and 30, a point subject boxed in so only the last ring is free. Assert hug_gap(placement.block, subject_ref) <= HUG_PX. And rings(30) is capped.
rules.risk_why: At the sizes in use (<= 14.5 pt for point captions) the cap never binds, so no map moves.

The one predicate is `lim` itself, stated once as KOSATSUBA_WAY_REACH_FT beside the other kosatsuba constants and read by the unit test (the gate test's 90 px was a separate, looser number: FR-003).
rules.fallback: L4's terminal. Where no verge takes a board, the board is not posted and meta.kosatsuba_dropped says why. That is GM-QUESTION-bound under L4, since 'no board' and 'a board off the way' are the two forms.

rules.rule: The notice board never stands more than FACING_DEG (45 degrees) off parallel to its nearest way (kosatsuba_faces_the_road).

FR-003: the test re-derives 'nearest' with its own loop in manifest order (lanes, then M['lane']) while the siter uses street_runs order, so at an exactly equidistant corner they can read different arms. The unit test calls _geom.ways.nearest_way_bearing. With the re-seat deleted, the 15-degree `_off_way` refusal and its loose fallback go with it.

rules.later_stages: None (the lanes are final before stage_notice).
rules.unit_test: A seat at an L-corner equidistant from both arms. Assert the board's rot equals nearest_way_bearing's tie-broken arm, and a seat beside a straggler crossing at 72 degrees takes the straggler's bearing.

rules.rule: The title placard never covers a building, plot, field, water, lane, label or the notice board (it may sit on cover) (title_clear_of_features; finish.py:543; tests/settlement/test_label_placement.py).
rows: R2 hamletgen/frame.py:stage_frame:412 (settlement/finish.py:title:348-368), the title band's placard over a runner
rules.mechanism: (a) The band rung: `band` is computed as today, then the placard's x is SCANNED along the band (step 8) with the same `_box_clear(obs)` the pocket and corner rungs use, instead of fixed at vx0+30. Failing that, a south band is tried. Failing both, the map's ink is clipped at the pre-band view's edge (a neatline: the band is title panel, outside the map). `_title_obstacles(window=map_view)` clips its polylines to the same window, so the predicate and the ink agree and the placard is over blank band by construction. (b) With no view: title() raises when `self.view` is unset (a precondition; both callers, frame.py:432 and rolling/roll.py:111, crop first, and the docstring already requires it). The canvas-center branch is deleted. (c) The stale stage_frame comment (frame.py:~405-412, 'falls back to a corner overlap') is corrected.
rules.fallback: The neatline clip in (a) is the terminal and always succeeds: a clipped band holds nothing. It is a map drawing convention (a title panel outside the map frame), recorded as such.
rules.later_stages: stage_notice runs AFTER the title (frame.py: stage_frame, then stage_notice), and place_kosatsuba's `_fits(..., top=26.0)` never consults M['title']. So a board can be posted under the placard. That is closed by adding the placard box (+4 ft) to place_kosatsuba's candidate filter (the caption already avoids it: label_obstacles includes M['title']).
rules.unit_test: A stub settlement whose four corners each hold a dry plot and a lane crossing the north edge at x = vx0+30..vx0+200. Assert the placard lands in the band and _box_clear holds on it. With lanes crossing the whole north and south edges, assert the clip is recorded and the placard box meets no clipped obstacle. title() with no view raises. place_kosatsuba on a map whose only verge lies under M['title']['placard'] does not seat there.
rules.retire: Nothing: the title's tests are already placer unit tests (tests/settlement/test_label_placement.py). If a hamletgen finished-map check of title_clear_of_features exists, it is retired with this.
rules.risk_why: Only rare maps reach the band. The clip is a new drawing convention on those maps. The board-under-placard filter can move a board on a map whose placard sits on a verge.

rules.rule: A caption on a GENERATED Mode A sheet (compound.py drafts) never lies on a feature it does not name (R3: 'Confirm the labels/ placer's cost blocks every built glyph on hamlets and the generated Mode A sheets').
rows: R3 future-work/cross-cutting.md: ## The caption-over-a-building rule was cut (generated Mode A half)
rules.mechanism: _seat_captions calls place(strict=True). Where it returns None, it runs labels/hand_sheet.py's `repair` (lift one neighbor and re-seat the pair), the mechanism feature 286 already uses on hand sheets, then retries with the frame's foot grown by CAPTION_ROOM steps (the canvas already grows to hug what is placed below it, compound.py:477-487). The one predicate is ObstacleIndex.cost == 0. Every drawn rect, wall band, gate post and caption is already an obstacle (compound.py emit_svg).
rules.fallback: The composer is seedless and deterministic: a program either has a clean seat for every caption after repair and growth, or it does not. The terminal is a ValueError from the composer naming the caption and the program, so the program's author changes the program. That is a raise at composition, before any sheet exists, not a finished-map check. It is listed under `impossible` for review because FR-002's wording forbids 'a raise'.
rules.later_stages: None: captions are seated last, after every drawn feature (compound.py emit_svg).
rules.unit_test: A two-building program whose small building's caption fits only over the large building's roof until the large building's own caption is lifted. Assert repair frees both at cost 0. And a program where one building is walled in with no free seat raises naming it.

rules.rule: A channel that declares a stream end never ends more than TRUNK_TOL (13 px) from that stream's drawn bed (channels_join_streams_at_confluence).
rules.owner: Two placers own it. l7r/diagram/settlement/fields/comb.py:_comb_source_channel (the intake end) and hamletgen/sink.py (the drain's brook_join end). hamletgen/frame.py:round_the_brooks is the later stage that can undo both. The census named only round_the_brooks.
rules.mechanism: (1) comb.py:~635-648 snaps the intake start onto the nearest stream centerline only when 0.5 < d <= 30. Otherwise the channel still declares frm=stream. The snap becomes unconditional for a channel declaring a stream end, and one that cannot reach within the rule does not declare it. (2) round_the_brooks holds, besides the taps, every stream vertex a declared channel end touches. Where the join lies mid-segment (brook_join walks at a stride), the join point is first inserted into the stream poly as a vertex and then held (round_stream's `hold` splits the fillet there). A held vertex coinciding with an existing corner would leave that corner unrounded, which the brook-bend rule forbids. In that case the channel's end is re-snapped to the rounded course (record and deferred ink, the regex path round_stream uses) instead of holding. The one predicate is `channel_end_on_stream(end, stream_poly, tol)` (the test's _poly_dist <= TRUNK_TOL), called after rounding by the stage's unit test.
rules.fallback: An intake that cannot reach a stream does not declare one. It is already sourced from the sluice/pond by the comb's other branches, so no form changes.
rules.later_stages: round_the_brooks is itself the later stage: closed by (2). No stage after stage_crossings moves a stream.
rules.unit_test: A stream with a 100-degree corner at w = 9, a drain whose brook_join lies exactly on that corner, and a second drain joining mid-segment 5 px from a corner's tangent point. After round_the_brooks, assert channel_end_on_stream for both, and that the corner is filleted. An intake whose source lies 45 px from the brook: assert it either snaps or does not declare frm=stream.
rules.retire: tests/gate/test_water_junctions.py::test_a_channel_declaring_a_stream_actually_reaches_its_bed. The module's `rolled` fixture is shared with the module's other tests, so the roll is freed only if every test in the module retires.
rules.risk_why: Touches the brook's rounding, which feature 261 reworked. Inserting held vertices changes fillet segmentation on maps with a drain confluence (Sawada).

rules.rule: No watercourse bed is ever painted above the topmost sheen (water composites as one surface; waterways_merge_at_crossings).
rules.mechanism: Already by construction: every water entry's bed is emitted into one group and every sheen into a later group, with bedz/sheenz taken from one running counter (finish.py:729-741). So min(sheenz) > max(bedz), recorded as water_bed_zmax / water_sheen_zmin. Nothing to change.
rules.unit_test: A Settlement with two streams, a drawn channel and a pond, run through finish(render=False). Assert M['water_sheen_zmin'] > M['water_bed_zmax'] and every record's bedz < every sheenz.

rules.rule: The pond fill is always painted above every course that joins the pond (pond_fill_covers_channel_mouths).
rules.mechanism: Already by construction: the bed group is emitted in `sorted(_entries, key=lambda w: bool(w.get('pond_fill')))`, a stable sort with the fill last (finish.py:729). So the fill's bedz exceeds every other bed's, joining or not. Nothing to change.
rules.unit_test: The L17 fixture with the channel's mouth inside the pond's rim and the pond fill registered FIRST. Assert pond_layer.bedz > that channel's bedz.

impossible.rule: L4-L7 + L2 + L11 terminal: a board with a clean caption is not guaranteed on every map without changing what the feature is.
impossible.reason: The placer seats a mandatory label (GM 2026-09-27) and every settlement carries a board (GM 2026-07-24). Where no verge in the view takes a board whose caption clears roofs, lanes, crowns and neighbors, one of the two rulings has to give: no board, or a caption that breaks a caption rule. Widening and the knob's affordances push this out to maps that may not exist, but the guarantee needs a stated terminal, and the choice is between distinct forms. GM-QUESTION, with a measurement first: cohort 1-48 plus the SC-003 probes, counting maps that reach the terminal.

impossible.rule: L15 terminal: a generated Mode A program with a caption that has no clean seat after repair and canvas growth.
impossible.reason: The composer is seedless, so the only exits are a raise naming the caption (the program's author fixes the program) or the standard's least-cost seat (a violation). FR-002 excludes 'a raise' literally, though that clause is aimed at finished-map checks that trigger a re-roll. This goes to review to confirm that a composition-time refusal counts.
